subject: Re: KMS/HSM: KEK wrapping, TLS negotiation, and rotation playbook

Subject: KMS/HSM: KEK wrapping and rotation questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our security RFP we'll need written answers on how Redwood handles key encryption key (KEK) wrapping for customer-controlled keys, TLS cipher negotiation and session affinity, and how key rotation is orchestrated when HSMs are involved. We want to understand both the high-level flow and specific algos/versions you support (e.g., RSA-OAEP-*/AESCBC/AES-GCM/KW).

Can you provide a short playbook we can include in our SOAR process that covers:
- BYOK import flow and verification (including attestation)
- Envelope encryption and KEK wrapping algorithms supported
- Rotation windows, rolling rewrap strategy, and blast-radius minimization
- TLS negotiation policy (ciphers, TLS versions, mTLS support) and how session affinity interacts with local KV caches
- Evidence and logs we can expect for audits (time-stamped rewrap events, HSM audit records)

Would prefer a single document plus any diagrams you can attach. Deadline: COB Friday (2027-11-05).

Thanks,
Alice

Subject: Re: KMS/HSM: KEK wrapping and rotation questions

Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is an initial playbook (medinfex_rfi_kms_answers_v1.pdf) and a schematic of our rotation/rewrap flow (rotation_diagram.png). Below is a concise summary to include directly in your SOAR ticket.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- BYOK/import: customer uploads an encrypted key packet to our ingestion endpoint. We support direct PKCS#11 import into an HSM-backed KEK or import as an encrypted envelope for our KMS to wrap. Attestation can be performed via an HSM-generated quote (TPM attestation for on-prem agents or HSM attestation sig for cloud HSM) and we provide signed attestation artifacts (SHA256 hash, timestamp, HSM module serial).
- Envelope & KEK algorithms: we support AES-GCM (AES-256-GCM) for envelope content encryption and AES Key Wrap (RFC 3394) or AES-KW with Padding (RFC 5649) for KEK wrapping. For asymmetric wrap during import we support RSA-OAEP with SHA-256 and RSA-OAEP-256.
- Rotation: rolling rewrap by key scope. Default rotation cadence is configurable (90 / 30 / 7 days). Rewrap runs as a staged job with per-tenant shard windows to limit blast radius; each rewrap operation records both pre/post key metadata and HSM audit record ids. Customers can opt-in to a forced re-encrypt (full data rewrap) or a lazy rewrap (future writes only).
- TLS & session affinity: TLS1.2 and TLS1.3 supported (we strongly prefer TLS1.3). Cipher policy defaults to a restricted set (see tls-cipher-list.txt) — ECDHE (X25519/P-256) key exchange with AES-128-GCM and AES-256-GCM suites, CHACHA20-POLY1305 available for mobile paths. Mutual TLS supported for private deployments and dedicated hosts (client cert validation + OCSP stapling). Session affinity is maintained at the routing plane; cached KV contents (prefix KVs) are sharded and persisted to local SSDs for warm starts. On failover, prefix caches are rebuilt from persisted checkpoints to avoid incorrect key usage.
- Audit evidence: for each rewrap we emit a signed event (ISO8601 timestamp, operator id, HSM slot id, HSM audit record pointer). For Dedicated/Private we provide downloadable HSM audit bundles and attestation artifacts. Hosted customers receive summarized audit logs via our Console and can request HSM audit extracts via an ATO process.

Attachments included: medinfex_rfi_kms_answers_v1.pdf (detailed Q&A), rotation_diagram.png (flow diagram), tls-cipher-list.txt (current allowed suites).

I'll let Dev and Rishi add ops-specific details below (scheduling, job-level controls, playbook snippets). If you'd like, we can convert the PDF into a single-page summary for your procurement pack.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Re: KMS/HSM: KEK wrapping and rotation questions

Hi Alice — quick operational notes to add to Evelyn's summary.

1) BYOK import flows (detailed):
- Option A (HSM direct import): Customer generates a keypair or symmetric key in their environment and performs a PKCS#11 or KMIP-backed import directly to the HSM. We support RSA and ECDSA private key imports, and symmetric key material via PKCS#11. The HSM enforces origin bits and marks keys as non-exportable if requested.
- Option B (Envelope import): Customer encrypts (client-side) the CEK with their KEK and uploads the envelope. Our KMS unwraps using configured KEK in the HSM and stores the CEK as an HSM-wrapped object.

2) Key wrap algos & selection:
- Envelope content: AES-256-GCM (recommended) or AES-128-GCM.
- KEK wrapping: AES-KW (RFC 3394) for symmetric KEK wrapping; for asymmetric imports we accept RSA-OAEP (SHA-256) and RSA-OAEP-256.
- We also support hybrid wraps (ECDH-ES + AES-GCM) for ephemeral import sessions when integrating with partner HSMs.

3) Rotation orchestration:
- Rewrap job pipeline: discover -> lock (per-tenant key-range) -> rewrap -> verify -> commit -> emit-event. Locks are optimistic with short TTLs to prevent global stalls. Rewrap jobs run in small windows with concurrency limits per region.
- Rollback: each step checkpoints metadata; if verification fails we revert to previous KEK metadata and mark the key for manual review.
- Blast-radius controls: tenant-level shard limits, per-run percentage (e.g., 5% of active keys), and pause-on-error thresholds.

4) TLS negotiation + session affinity details:
- Termination: Hosted API endpoints terminate TLS at the edge (NGINX + Envoy) configured to prefer TLS1.3. We reject known-weak ciphers and TLS1.0/1.1.
- Session affinity: our routing uses consistent-hash routing keyed by customer-id + route. Affinity is sticky for the session TTL and routed pods maintain a local KV cache; on pod drain we stream cache checkpoints to the replacement pod.

5) Audit & evidence:
- For each rewrap event we store: event id, timestamp, old key version id, new key version id, HSM audit sequence id, operator (system or API client id), and a SHA-256 digest of the envelope. PDF contains sample audit record lines.

If you want, I can include a sample automation runbook snippet (Ansible/Runbook) that triggers a safe rewrap.

-Dev
Software Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Dev,

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering security reviewer:

1) For RSA-OAEP imports, can Redwood confirm whether it supports OAEP with MGF1-SHA256 (RSA-OAEP-256) and the maximum modulus sizes supported? We need to avoid 1024/2048-only constraints.

2) During rolling rewrap we want explicit guarantees that old key material cannot be used for new decrypt operations after the rewrap completes (i.e., atomic cutover per-key). How does your commit step ensure atomicity across distributed stores?

3) For TLS session resumption: does Redwood use session tickets (stateless) or session IDs (server state)? If session tickets, how are ticket keys rotated and protected (HSM?) — we need assurance they're not stored in plaintext on nodes.

4) Evidence: can you provide a one-line example (log entry) with the fields you mentioned (event id, hsm seq id, old/new key ids)?

Appreciate the quick clarification — these will be included in our risk assessment.

Regards,
M. Lopez
Head of Security Engineering, MedInfex
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: M. Lopez <security-lead@medinfex.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS/HSM: KEK wrapping and rotation questions

M. Lopez — quick answers inline to your numbered points.

1) RSA-OAEP: we support RSA-OAEP with MGF1 using SHA-256 and SHA-512 (OAEP-256 and OAEP-512). We support modulus sizes up to 8192 bits for imports when the HSM vendor allows it; common supported sizes are 2048/3072/4096. We document vendor-specific limits in the onboarding pack; for Dedicated/Private customers we can expose exact HSM module capabilities (e.g., Thales Luna 7xxx, AWS Nitro HSM) during provisioning.

2) Atomic rewrap: our rewrap job performs a two-phase commit at the KMS metadata layer: 1) write new KEK metadata and new key-version pointer into a durable metadata store (with pre-commit marker), 2) verify HSM audit entries and successful rewrap, 3) flip the live pointer to the new version and garbage-collect the old only after successful verification. The flip is an atomic pointer swap in the metadata service; all decrypt APIs read the pointer under a read lock ensuring no interleaving reads of mixed versions. For distributed reads we use a consistent version tag propagated with requests; if a request arrives mid-flip it will be served by the version referenced by the tag or retried. This guarantees the old material cannot be used for new decrypts after commit.

3) Session resumption: we use TLS1.3 session tickets by default for hosted endpoints. Ticket encryption keys are stored in the KMS and protected by the HSM; ticket keys are themselves KEK-wrapped objects. Rotation of ticket keys is performed on a rolling schedule and follows the same rewrap orchestration (small windows, shard limits). Tickets are not persisted in plaintext on application nodes — nodes cache a ticket decryption key in memory only and fetch rotated ticket-key material from the KMS when necessary. For Dedicated/Private deployments with mTLS enabled, tickets can be disabled and server-side session IDs used if required.

4) Sample log entry (audit):
EVENT_ID=evt-20271104-0009 | TIMESTAMP=2027-11-04T15:58:32Z | OP=key_rewrap | TENANT=medinfex | OLD_KEY=key_v42 | NEW_KEY=key_v43 | HSM_AUDIT_SEQ=HSMAUD:6789123 | OPERATOR=system-scheduled-rewrap | DIGEST=sha256:3f8b9a... | VERIFY=PASS

If you want a signed bundle with HSM audit slices, indicate the timeframe and we'll prepare a time-limited download (includes signed attestation and the HSM sequence references).

I'll update the diagram with the atomic cutover note and regenerate the PDF if you'd like an annotated copy.

Thanks — Rishi
